children: Crude contracts were down about $1 around midday Tuesday, as the oil market paused the significant rally it saw over the past two weeks on the prospect that U.S.-Iran diplomacy could bring an end to the almost eight-month-old Middle East conflict.
At noon ET, the more-active December NYMEX West Texas Intermediate contract was down about $1 to $97.55/bbl and November WTI was about 95cts lower to $102.70/bbl.
London-based December ICE Brent was down $1.15 to $108.40/bbl and January Brent was $1.25 lower to $104.80/bbl.

December RBOB contracts were down 8.45cts to $3.0205/gal and November RBOB was 10.2cts lower at $3.0895/gal. December ULSD was 0.4ct lower at $4.7225/gal, while November ULSD was up 2.45cts to $4.946/gal.
WTI futures were initially up by as much as $2, driven by supply fears amid Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian infrastructure.
However, some energy investors opted to take profits later. WTI prices had risen more than $10 in the last two weeks on heightened fears of an escalating Iran war.
